edits.english: MISHNA: With regard to Jewish craftsmen (i.e., Israelites) to whom a gentile sent a barrel of wine used for a libation in lieu of their wage (in exchange for their work), and this wine is forbidden for benefit — it is permitted for them to say to him: Give us its monetary value, how much the barrel is worth. But once the barrel has entered into their possession, it is prohibited for them to say so, as that would be tantamount to selling libation wine to the gentile and deriving benefit from its value.

edits.hebrew: מותר לומר לו תן לנו את דמיה - דהא לא קנו לה, והוא אינו חייב להן אלא מעות. ותניא לעיל (עבודה זרה דף סד.): ישראל שנושה בעובד כוכבים מנה, מכר עבודת כוכבים והביא לו יין נסך, והביא לו — מותר:

edits.english: It is permitted for them to say to him: Give us its monetary value - for the Jewish craftsmen did not acquire the barrel, and the gentile owes them only money. And it was taught above (Avodah Zarah 64a): If an Israelite was owed a *maneh* by a gentile, and the gentile sold an idol and brought the Israelite wine used for a libation, it is permitted for the Israelite to accept it.

Jewish laborers who performed work for a gentile, and the gentile sent them a barrel of wine as their wage: if they had not yet accepted it as their wage, it is permitted for them to say to him: 'Instead of sending us this barrel, let it be yours, and you give us its monetary value' (Ran). But if they accepted it as their wage, it is forbidden (R' Yerucham and Rosh). (And see below, section 123, that even after accepting it, it is permitted nowadays).

MISHNA: Jewish craftsmen (meaning, Israelites) to whom a gentile sent a barrel of wine used for a libation as their wage (in exchange for their work), and it is forbidden for benefit — it is permitted for them to say to him: “Give us its monetary value,” how much the barrel is worth. But if the barrel has entered their possession — it is forbidden to receive its value from the gentile, for this is as if they sold libation wine and benefited from its value.

And not only because the barrel did not reach the Jewish craftsmen's hands and they did not acquire it, but also the money the Jewish craftsmen receive from the gentile is not in exchange for the barrel, because the gentile owes them only money for their wage. And the Ra'avad wrote that if the gentile stipulated with the Jewish craftsmen to give them wine as their wage, then he owes them wine.
